name: Rescue Mission
definition: A protagonist or team enters danger to recover people who remain active participants, while urgency tests duty, attachment, and the cost of bringing everyone home.
negative_signals: recovery of an object rather than a person
diagnostic_questions: Is another person's recovery the organizing objective?
Can the endangered person affect the rescue rather than function as cargo?

neighbors.distinction: Rescue foregrounds entry and recovery by outsiders while escape foregrounds captives defeating confinement.
A rescue may use military methods, but its success is measured by lives recovered.

reader_promises.name: Human objective
reader_promises.description: Make the endangered person's identity, agency, and relationship matter beyond mission success.

reader_promises.name: Urgent extraction
reader_promises.description: Create changing hazards that make entry, contact, and return distinct problems.

roles.name: Rescuer
roles.description: Accepts responsibility for reaching and returning with the endangered person.

roles.name: Endangered person
roles.description: Survives, resists, signals, negotiates, or complicates assumptions about rescue.

roles.name: Obstructor
roles.description: Actively prevents recovery or exploits the rescue attempt.

stakes: Trust between rescuer and endangered person
motifs: Routes that work only one way

movements.name: Call to recover
movements.description: Define who is endangered, what is known, and why action cannot wait.

movements.name: Dangerous approach
movements.description: Reach the person while learning that initial intelligence is incomplete.

movements.name: Contact
movements.description: Let the endangered person's choices change the objective or extraction method.

movements.name: Extraction
movements.description: Return through consequences created by entry, contact, and opposition.

complications.name: Objective multiplies
complications.description: More people require help than the available route or resources support.

complications.name: Rescue refused
complications.description: The endangered person has a reason not to accept the proposed extraction.

complications.name: Return route lost
complications.description: The approach method cannot carry the rescued party back.

twists.name: Wrong location
twists.description: The apparent holding site is a transfer point or deliberate lure.

twists.name: Rescue changes the conflict
twists.description: Recovering the person releases information, authority, or danger that alters the larger struggle.

conclusions.name: Home together
conclusions.description: Rescuer and recovered person return through earned cooperation.

conclusions.name: Partial recovery
conclusions.description: Some lives are saved while an explicit choice defines the loss.

conclusions.name: Enabled self-rescue
conclusions.description: The intervention succeeds by restoring the endangered person's agency rather than carrying them out.

variation_axes.question: What binds rescuer and endangered person?

subversions: Make the endangered person the better strategist after contact.
Define success as restoring choice rather than relocating a body.
cliches_to_avoid: A passive hostage with no interior objective
quality_checks: The endangered person affects at least one decisive plan change.
Approach and extraction create different challenges.
The outcome resolves the relationship as well as physical safety.

sources.title: The Team Film Genre
sources.contribution: Provides team-objective, preparation, execution, weakness, and coda patterns.

sources.title: Aphorisms for Writing Science Fiction
sources.author_or_organization: Science Fiction and Fantasy Writers Association
sources.contribution: Supports causal character action, dramatic economy, thematic climax, and consistent scale.
